item.title: Amwins Acquires Firearms MGA Chiarello
item.description: Chiarello will join Amwins Underwriting, adding a specialized program portfolio serving firearms manufacturers, distributors, retailers, hunting and shooting clubs, instructors, ammunition manufacturers and accessories businesses, according to an Amwins statement. (Image credit: IIR.) Amwins (Charlotte, N.C.) has acquired Joseph Chiarello & Co. “Chiarello has built the gold standard in a highly technical, often overlooked niche,” comments Ryan Armijo, President, Amwins Underwriting.

item.title: Labor Day Travelers Face Higher Costs, Heavier Traffic: AAA
item.description: Labor Day travelers face heavier traffic, higher fuel, airfare, and hotel costs this year, according to AAA. The Top Labor Day Travel Destinations for 2026: Seattle, WA Orlando, FL Boston, MA Denver, CO New York, NY Chicago, IL Anaheim/Los Angeles, CA Las Vegas, NV Anchorage, AK Atlanta, GA Rome, Italy Vancouver, Canada London, England Dublin, Ireland Paris, France Calgary, Canada Barcelona, Spain Athens, Greece Amsterdam, Netherlands Halifax, Canada Labor Day Travel Costs Rise for Flights and Hotels Travelers are paying more for several major components of a Labor Day vacation this year. For travelers flying to the most popular Labor Day destinations, airfare is nearly 20% higher than last year, averaging $790.

item.title: AIG Executive Chair and Former CEO Zaffino Set to Exit for Palantir
item.description: AIG said early Wednesday that its former chief executive officer and current executive chair Peter Zaffino will be leaving the board effective Sept. Zaffino had just transitioned to the position of executive chair on June 1. To take his place on the board, AIG said John Rice, lead independent director, will serve as chair when Zaffino departs.

item.title: Former Apple Engineers’ Physical AI Startup Lyte Raises $165M At $1.6B Valuation
item.description: Lyte , a physical AI startup building sensing and perception technology for robots, has raised $165 million in Series C funding at a $1.6 billion post-money valuation. The Sunnyvale, California-based company was founded in 2021 by Alexander Shpunt , Arman Hajati and Yuval Gerson — a trio of former Apple engineers who worked on the iPhone giant’s advanced sensing and perception technologies. Shpunt had also previously co-founded PrimeSense , a startup whose 3D-sensing technology powered Microsoft Kinect before Apple acquired the company in 2013.

item.title: US and Bermuda reinsurers maintain profitability as premium growth slows: AM Best
item.description: AM Best, the credit rating agency and provider of insurance industry data and analysis, has reported that a group of leading US and Bermuda reinsurers remained underwriting profitable for a fifth consecutive year in 2025, despite a significant slowdown in premium growth. The findings are contained in AM Best’s latest Best’s Market Segment Report, US & Bermuda Reinsurers Maintain Strong Performance Despite Softening Market . AM Best said the sharp reduction in growth reflects a more cautious approach from reinsurers as market conditions become softer.

item.title: People: Builders Insurance Names Jasmund Board Chairman
item.description: Atlanta-based Builders Insurance Group has named David Jasmund, a longtime board member and investment banker, as chairman of the board. Jasmund has served on the Builders board since 2009. Jasmund succeeds Charles Potok, who retired last month after three years as chairman, the company said in a news release.

item.title: US-Iran Clashes Escalate as Fears Grow of Extended Conflict
item.description: Fighting between the US and Iran over control of the Strait of Hormuz intensified after a period of relative calm, triggering a fresh jump in energy prices as fears grow of an open-ended war. The US military carried out a second round of strikes in three days overnight, targeting radar systems and mine-laying capabilities along Iran’s southern coast. Iran retaliated with drone and missile volleys on US bases across the Middle East, in line with a pattern used throughout the six-month war.

item.title: Amwins Acquires Firearms Insurance Specialist Joseph Chiarello & Co.
item.description: Specialty insurance wholesale broker Amwins reports it has acquired Joseph Chiarello & Co., Inc., a managing general agent (MGA) specializing in commercial insurance for the firearms industry. Founded in 1934 and now led by third-generation family members Joseph and Stephen Chiarello, the company has spent more than 40 years building its reputation in firearms industry insurance, serving more than 4,000 businesses. Chiarello will join Amwins Underwriting, adding a new area of specialty expertise to the division’s program portfolio.

item.title: Root and Carvana extend embedded insurance partnership to 2028
item.description: Root Insurance has announced the extension of its embedded partnership with Carvana to at least August 2028. Alex Timm, founder and chief executive officer of Root Insurance, said the renewal reflected the strength of the programme. In less than four years, the partnership has surpassed 200,000 policies sold.

item.title: Insurance's Gap in Identity Security
item.description: Partner ecosystems are the identity security gap that most financial institutions, including insurers, have yet to close. Research from Enterprise Strategy Group (ESG) , commissioned by Thales, found that 74% of BFSI organizations, spanning banking, insurance, and financial services, report third-party identities growing faster than employee identities, with third-party identity volumes projected to grow 37% over the next 12 months. The operational signals emerging from partner identity environments increasingly look like security warnings.

item.title: Root and Carvana extend partnership
item.description: Root Insurance announced the extension of its embedded partnership with Carvana to at least August 2028. In less than four years, the partnership surpassed 200,000 policies sold. We’re so excited about what this means for today’s car shoppers and how they can finally have a delightful purchase experience.” – Alex Timm, Founder & CEO of Root Insurance.

item.title: Chariot Re raises $700 million to expand life and annuity reinsurance platform
item.description: The Bermuda-based Class E life and annuity reinsurer plans to use the financing to expand its capacity for a growing pipeline of reinsurance opportunities. The financing expands our capacity to scale the reinsurance platform while maintaining our focus on disciplined underwriting and policyholder protection.” – Cynthia Smith, Chief Executive Officer of Chariot Re. MetLife and General Atlantic, Chariot Re’s sponsors, participated in the round, alongside institutional investors led by Chubb.

item.title: Zing Health taps debt for $30 million raise
item.description: That marks a departure from Zing’s previous equity rounds, including a $140 million raise in September 2024 from a group that included Newlight Partners, Town Hall Ventures, CRG, Leavitt Equity Partners, First Trust Capital Partners, and Health 2047 Capital Partners. Zing Health , the Chicago Medicare Advantage insurer co-founded in 2019 by Dr. Two related entities, Zing Health Consolidator, Inc.

item.title: Insurity Adds KMG Integration Partner
item.description: “KMG adds valuable system integration capacity, insurance knowledge, and a customer-focused approach that will help extend our reach and support successful outcomes for insurers and MGAs using Insurity solutions, including Insurity Pro Suite.” KMG supports insurance organizations with business and technology transformation initiatives. (Image credit: IIR.) Insurity (Hartford, Conn.) has entered a strategic integration relationship with Key Management Group (KMG; Jericho, N.Y.), an insurance-focused consulting and technology services firm. “Our partner ecosystem plays an essential role in how we help customers modernize with less friction and stronger execution,” comments Jeff Weiner, AVP, SI Alliances and Partnerships, Insurity.

item.title: First Electric Range Rover Will Cost Buyers More Than $200,000
item.description: Jaguar Land Rover Automotive Plc’s first electric Range Rover will start at £154,070 ($208,420), a price tag that will test wealthy buyers’ appetites for a battery-powered sport utility vehicle. Orders are now open for what is one of the most expensive electric SUVs on the market and almost £50,000 more than the standard combustion-engine version. The Range Rover Electric can travel 372 miles (599 kilometers) on a single charge in testing conditions, and goes from 10% to 80%-charged in 22 minutes.

item.title: Government Backs OpenAI in New York Times Copyright Case
item.description: The Trump administration has filed a brief supporting OpenAI in its dispute with the New York Times and several other newspapers over the company’s use of their work to train the large language models behind ChatGPT, saying AI training generally makes fair use of copyrighted material. The case is one of dozens brought by copyright holders against tech companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta Platforms for what they say is misuse of their material to train AI systems. government has weighed in on a wave of cases brought by copyright owners including authors, publishers, music labels and news outlets over AI training, in a development that could bolster tech companies as they fight the claims.

item.title: Investigators Find Washington Chemical Tank Called Unfit for Service Before Deadly Failure
item.description: An inspection contractor found a chemical tank at a Washington state paper mill “not fit for continued service” 10 months before it failed in May, killing 11 in one of the deadliest U.S. Chemical Safety Board’s update about the May 26 failure in Longview, which expelled enough caustic liquid to blow out building walls, is part of an ongoing investigation. The federal agency said it is still determining the cause of the failure.

item.title: Blackout Risk Rises as Heat Wave Stresses Largest U.S. Electric Grids
item.description: The risk of power outages is expected to escalate across a broad swath of the United States on Wednesday as intense heat will test the capacity of electricity supplies serving millions of homes and businesses from the Midwest through the Mid-Atlantic. Department of Energy warned of the potential for heightened blackout risks in the PJM Interconnection, the largest U.S. In the Ozark region of rural Missouri, the Howell-Oregon Electric Cooperative advised customers to unplug unused chargers and appliances due to the continued extreme heat.

item.title: Marsh Launches $10B Property Insurance Exchange Stratus
item.description: Marsh announced the launch of Stratus on August 26, a property insurance exchange designed to address the complex operational risks of digital infrastructure projects including data centers and associated critical support systems. “By combining Marsh’s engineering data and analytics, risk consulting capabilities, and access to the global (re)insurance and capital markets, Stratus is designed to improve the quality and efficiency of operational digital infrastructure property placements and help clients secure the protection they need to support growth at scale.” Stratus provides access to up to $10 billion in property insurance capacity on a single-placement basis through the global property risk transfer market. Stratus will also leverage Marsh’s data and analytics and advisory services to help clients procure customized property coverage as they transition their digital infrastructure assets into operation.

item.title: The IPO Window Is Closing. Here Are 8 Startups To Watch.
item.description: With the year’s end now in sight, a small window remains for other startups to launch 2026 IPOs. With that, here’s a look at notable venture-backed startups that Crunchbase’s predictive intelligence suggests are potential IPO candidates within the next six months. Now, with the public-market window narrowing and the post-Labor Day filing sprint upon us, attention is turning to which venture-backed companies might still make a move in coming months.

item.title: India’s NCDEX expands parametric weather derivative offering to Chennai rainfall
item.description: The National Commodity and Derivatives Exchange (NCDEX) has expanded its range of parametric weather derivative products, launching a futures contract to enable participants to hedge the financial exposure of rainfall extremes and variability in the city of Chennai and surrounding area. The NCDEX explains why Chennai is an important and relevant location for weather hedging, “Chennai, one of India’s largest metropolitan and industrial centers, is uniquely exposed to rainfall variability due to its dependence on the Northeast Monsoon (September to December), which contributes the majority of the city’s annual rainfall. It’s the second location in India where rainfall weather derivatives are now available, after the NCDEX launched its first contract for Mumbai back in May this year .

item.title: MetLife and General Atlantic sidecar Chariot Re secures $700m in third capital raise
item.description: The financing expands our capacity to scale the reinsurance platform while maintaining our focus on disciplined underwriting and policyholder protection.” Michel Khalaf, President and Chief Executive Officer of MetLife, said: “Chariot Re’s third capital raise reflects the confidence investors have in the platform we’ve built with General Atlantic and the Chariot Re management team. in partnership with investor General Atlantic, has closed an oversubscribed third capital raise of approximately $700 million in equity and debt financing, with backing from a group of leading institutional investors, including Chubb. Both MetLife and General Atlantic, who serve as Chariot Re’s exclusive asset managers, participated in the financing, bringing together deep expertise in insurance, retirement, and global investment.

item.title: No longer alternative, how capital sources can work together is the strategic decision: Gallagher Re
item.description: “For many of our largest clients, deciding how much risk sits with traditional markets, how much sits with capital markets, and how those different sources of capacity work together has become a core strategic decision.” Thompson said that, in addition to asking what the most efficient structure for the renewal is, clients are increasingly asking what the most efficient way to finance that risk over the next three to five years is. During reinsurance broker Gallagher Re’s Pre-Monte Carlo Media Briefing, Will Thompson, Head of Global Clients, said alternative capital is no longer a separate conversation from traditional reinsurance and is now an integral part of the capital stack. Alternative capital is no longer a separate conversation.

item.title: Stable T&Cs ahead of 1.1, but hurricane season and other factors hold leverage: Moody’s
item.description: Reinsurance terms and conditions (T&Cs) are likely to hold heading to January 1, 2027, renewals, Moody’s analysts commented following the release of their Sector In-Depth and Outlook reports. While 2026 has experienced relatively moderate loss activity to date, the North Atlantic hurricane season is yet to be over, with its peak usually expected from late August to September. Underwriting discipline has remained stable in 2026, even as reinsurers continue to grow their exposure to natural catastrophe risk.

item.title: MS Reinsurance names Julien Mollinier as CUO, Global Speciality Lines
item.description: Zurich-domiciled reinsurer MS Reinsurance (MS Re), part of global insurance group MS&AD, has appointed Julien Mollinier as Chief Underwriting Officer (CUO), Global Speciality Lines. Bruniecki commented, “Julien brings a strong blend of strategic leadership, as well as technical and broad market experience, all of which will be invaluable to strengthen our Global Speciality Lines team and business. In his new role, Mollinier will lead MS Re’s Global Speciality team, and drive its strategic development.

item.title: Peak Re appoints Sanjiv Agarwal as Head of Operations
item.description: Peak Re, a global reinsurance company providing risk solutions and services to insurance and financial services clients, has appointed Sanjiv Agarwal as Head of Operations as the company continues to implement its growth and transformation strategy, which took effect on 1 September 2026. Agarwal joins Peak Re with nearly 30 years of experience across operations, transformation, technology and people leadership within the financial services sector. Based in Hong Kong, Agarwal will be responsible for Peak Re’s operations functions, including Technical Accounting, Claims and Technology.

item.title: People Moves: Cincinnati Insurance Chief Claims Officer Schambow to Retire, McMillan to Assume Responsibilities
item.description: Schambow , CPCU, AIM, ASLI, chief claims officer for its property casualty subsidiaries, led by The Cincinnati Insurance Company, will retire in January 2027. Schambow has served as Cincinnati’s top claims officer since 2020, capping a nearly 40-year career with the company. Schambow became the first claims manager for The Cincinnati Specialty Underwriters Insurance Company in 2007 and transitioned to lead the field claims team in 2014.

item.title: Severe Thunderstorms Threaten From Great Lakes to New Jersey
item.description: Another round of severe thunderstorms is threatening the US and Canada, from the Great Lakes to New Jersey, promising to disrupt flights and cause power outages. There is a level two risk of severe thunderstorms from Michigan to New Jersey on Wednesday, the US Storm Prediction Center said, with the potential for southern New York to be hit in the evening. Yesterday, dozens of trees and power lines were knocked down across the state and New Jersey, while hundreds of flights were canceled.

item.title: Florida Citizens Awards Commercial Clearinghouse Management to Bridge Specialty
item.description: Despite months of lobbying and significant political campaign contributions by Ryan Turner Specialty brokerage, the winning bid for management of part of a Florida Citizens Property Insurance commercial clearinghouse has been awarded to another brokerage. At a meeting Tuesday, Citizens officials announced that the contract for the controversial clearinghouse manager for commercial policy depopulation was awarded to Bridge Specialty Wholesale, a division of the Brown & Brown, the national brokerage headquartered in Daytona Beach. Some in the Florida insurance industry early this year pointed out that Chicago-based Ryan Turner, part of a national brokerage and distribution company, had lobbied for the legislation that required Citizens to establish the commercial clearinghouse, perhaps in an effort to position Ryan as the manager of the system.

item.title: Peter Zaffino to join Palantir as global head of financial services
item.description: Palantir Technologies has announced that Peter Zaffino will join the company as global head of financial services, effective 15 January 2027. Zaffino, previously chief executive officer and executive chairman of AIG, will drive growth and “transformational impact” across Palantir’s financial services business. I am incredibly excited to work with financial services organizations to transform their AI strategy into strategic advantage,” said Zaffino.

item.title: Building a Modern Claims Organization: Gina Reyes’ Playbook for an Increasingly Complex Claims Landscape
item.description: The post Building a Modern Claims Organization: Gina Reyes’ Playbook for an Increasingly Complex Claims Landscape appeared first on Coverager - Insurance news and insights . Drawing on her experience building the organization from the ground up, Gina offers a practical playbook for what modern claims leaders should prioritize as complexity continues to rise. Gina’s experience building Openly’s claims organization from the ground up offers a practical framework for navigating that reality: Hire adjusters with the expertise and empathy increasingly complex claims demand.

item.title: Aviva launches Premier for larger UK commercial clients
item.description: “Aviva Premier follows the refocusing of our UK Commercial Lines business and supports our ambition to grow with larger and more complex UK clients. Aviva has launched Aviva Premier, a commercial insurance proposition for larger mid-market businesses with more complex risks. The launch follows a refocusing of Aviva’s UK Commercial Lines business, as the insurer targets growth among larger and more complex commercial clients.

item.title: BHSI launches surety in France
item.description: Berkshire Hathaway Specialty Insurance has launched a surety business in France and appointed Stéphane Fauré as head of surety for the country. Based in Paris, Fauré will lead the development of surety solutions for brokers and customers, targeting upper middle-market and large corporate clients. Fauré brings more than 10 years of experience in surety and guarantees, including work in regional strategy, business transformation, product development, and broker and bank relationships.

item.title: Juan Antonio Costa vuelve a la consultoría aseguradora de la mano de Atos Amplify
item.description: Atos Amplify ha incorporado a Juan Antonio Costa Leo como Consulting Partner for Insurance para Iberia, con el objetivo de reforzar su negocio de consultoría especializado en el sector asegurador.

item.title: Eiopa refuerza la confianza en el mercado único con la armonización de los sistemas de garantía de seguros
item.description: Eiopa ha remitido a la Comisión Europea su asesoramiento técnico sobre estándares mínimos comunes para los sistemas de garantía de seguros (IGS, por sus siglas en inglés) en la Unión Europea.

item.title: Vanesa Ibáñez Furió, nueva Interim Director Southern Europe de Crawford & Company
item.description: Con efecto de ayer, 1 de septiembre, Crawford & Company ha anunciado a su organización el nombramiento de Vanesa Ibáñez Furió como Interim Director Southern Europe. Se va a hacer público al mercado a lo largo del día de hoy.

item.title: OpenAI Says Upcoming Model Is So Capable It Requires Stronger Guardrails
item.description: OpenAI has determined that one of its upcoming models is so capable it requires additional safety measures before it can be launched. The model, called Astra, can spot more security vulnerabilities than the most advanced OpenAI model publicly available today, company officials told reporters on a conference call on Tuesday. Astra is the first OpenAI model to trigger the tougher safeguards mandated by the company’s safety protocol, a threshold that, until now, had remained theoretical.

item.title: Judge Throws Out Bulk of Economic Claims Over Baltimore Bridge Tragedy
item.description: A federal judge has agreed with the owner and manager of the Dali cargo ship responsible for the collapse of Baltimore’s Key Bridge that the bulk of the remaining claims against them for economic damage are invalid. Ship Owner Seeks Dismissal of Economic Loss Claims From Baltimore Bridge Collapse The Francis Scott Key Bridge collapsed in the early morning hours of March 26, 2024, after being struck by the Dali as the vessel departed the Port of Baltimore. In addition to dismissing other claims by Baltimore city and county, the ruling throws out unsettled claims for private economic damages by longshoremen, energy, export, manufacturing, construction services, technology, sugar, molasses and publishing firms along with related insurers including Markel, Liberty Mutual, QBE, AXA XL, Evanston and Canopius.

item.title: Northern Re grows in-force premium since launch to more than $1 billion
item.description: Since its launch, the organisation has reportedly written more than 100 bespoke reinsurance contracts across treaty, legacy and whole-account, including retrocession, and structured solutions. Northern Re, the collateralized reinsurance company that provides investors with access to the returns of its long-tail casualty underwriting business, has now surpassed the $1 billion of in-force premiums milestone. While Northern Re’s average line size is around $20 million, the company said it selectively deploys “more than $100 million on individual opportunities where conviction is highest,” which suggests at least one opportunity at that scale exists in the portfolio today.

item.title: Cat bond and ILS market well-positioned for disciplined, continued growth: Artemis London 2026
item.description: The catastrophe bond and insurance-linked securities market remains well-positioned, even as reinsurance market conditions soften, with speakers at our Artemis London 2026 conference yesterday highlighting the discipline in the market and that this is expected to persist, while growth opportunities are still evident. We held our Artemis London 2026 conference on September 1st and had around 220 attendees through the door on the day. This was our fifth conference in the Artemis London series and a particularly engaging one, as the current state of the market made for very interesting and forward-looking discussions on stage and during the valuable networking sessions with attendees.

item.title: Industry to experience average annual insured nat cat losses of $171bn: Verisk
item.description: According to Verisk, the global data analytics and technology provider, the insurance industry should be prepared to withstand an average $171 billion in annual natural catastrophe losses in any given year, according to the firm’s latest average annual losses (AAL) benchmark. This information stems from Verisk’s 2026 Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses Report, which revealed that severe thunderstorm accounts for 40% of modeled insured catastrophe risk, which is more than any other peril. The figure is up $19 billion on Verisk’s 2025 benchmark, due to continued growth in property and insured values worldwide.

item.title: Marsh and Resilience introduce Cyber Protect across Asia
item.description: Marsh, a global insurance broker and risk adviser, has partnered with cyber risk management company Resilience to launch Cyber Protect in Asia, an offering aimed at helping organisations identify significant cyber exposures before they result in financial losses. The solution is available exclusively through Marsh in Asia and brings together Marsh’s cyber insurance expertise with Resilience’s Risk Operations Center (ROC). The service is included within the Cyber Protect programme at no additional cost to eligible clients, according to Marsh and Resilience.

item.title: Video: Adequate pricing is key as risk landscape evolves, says Urs Baertschi, Swiss Re
item.description: Today’s risk landscape is more connected and faster moving, and as the environment continues to evolve, what’s important across the re/insurance value chain is charging an adequate rate, according to Urs Baertschi, Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Property & Casualty (P&C) Reinsurance at Swiss Re. Watch the full video interview to hear more from Swiss Re’s Baertschi on the competitive market landscape, evolving risk landscape, the 2026 renewals, AI and technology, and more. “At the end of the day, what’s important for the entire industry throughout the entire value chain to remember is that in that evolving risk landscape, it’s important to charge an adequate rate,” said Baertschi.

item.title: Lloyd’s reinsurance pricing softens, but AM Best sees adequate rates through 2026
item.description: The Lloyd’s reinsurance market is facing intensifying softening pressures in 2026, particularly across property catastrophe business, although rates have declined from a very strong peak and are still expected to remain adequate, according to AM Best. Despite the deterioration, the rating agency said rates have moderated from a “very strong peak” and are expected to remain adequate through at least the end of 2026. During the first half of this year, most reinsurance lines are said to have experienced declines in risk-adjusted pricing, with pressure most pronounced in property catastrophe business, particularly for US-exposed risks, while AM Best also noted pressure on terms and conditions.

item.title: Judge Says Smucker’s Lawsuit Against Trader Joe’s Over Frozen PB&J Can Proceed
item.description: Smucker can proceed with a lawsuit against Trader Joe’s over frozen sandwiches that Smucker claims are too similar to its Uncrustables. Smucker sued Trader Joe’s in federal court in Ohio last fall, claiming Trader Joe’s committed a trademark violation when it introduced frozen peanut butter and jelly sandwiches with the same round shape and crimped edges as Uncrustables. Related: Smucker Sues Trader Joe’s, Saying New PB&Js Are Too Much Like Uncrustables The lawsuit further alleged that Trader Joe’s put its crustless PB&Js peanut in packaging that too closely resembled the coloring of an Uncrustables box and featured a similar photograph of a sandwich with a bite taken out of one side.

item.title: Fatal Floods Expose Threats to Hydropower in the Roof of the World
item.description: The devastating deluge that swept through the mountain valleys on the border between Nepal and Tibet in China is a potent reminder of a growing green-energy risk in one of the world’s most hazard-prone areas.Hydropower dams high in the Himalayas seem to be a ready solution for an energy-starved region. “Hydropower is very important for climate change adaptation and the energy transition,” said Holger Frey, a researcher leading a group studying hazards and risks in mountains at the University of Zürich. “This is a dilemma for countries investing in renewables and hydro, and at the same time having to deal with the consequences of climate change.” The region has already had warnings, including a glacier collapse in the Indian state of Uttarakhand in 2021 that left at least 200 dead or missing, and floods in Pakistan that left a third of the country under water in 2022.

item.title: Germany Blames Russia for Attempted Drone Attack, Expects More
item.description: Germany’s government said an investigation found that Russia is behind a failed drone attack at an airport in Leipzig last month and that the Kremlin is likely to step up hybrid aggression. “On the contrary: with the attempted attack in Leipzig, the Russian leadership has deliberately chosen to inflict further significant damage on our already severely strained bilateral relationship.” The move by German authorities marks a significant deterioration in relations between Berlin and Moscow more than four years after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Chancellor Friedrich Merz had said last week that the attempted drone attack on the logistics hub for deliveries to Ukraine represented a new level of hybrid warfare — and perpetrators “will pay a price.” Germany will get “a fitting response” to its decisions on closing Russian facilities, Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova told the state-run Tass news service.
